withShortcut.description: A control's tooltip or name with its first keyboard shortcut in brackets: {text} is the tooltip, {keys} the keycaps ("Ctrl + Z"), which stay as they are.

orPress.description: A hint followed by the shortcut that does the same: {text} is the hint ("Double-click to add text"), {keys} the keycaps.

reviewHint.description: Added to the end of a notice after automatic changes: Review mode lists them, opened with {keys}. Starts with the full stop that ends the notice's sentence.

reviewHintNoKey.description: Added to the end of a notice after automatic changes when Review mode has no shortcut. Starts with the full stop that ends the notice's sentence.

undoHint.lead.description: Added to the end of a notice after a big change: the Undo shortcut. Starts with a space and a middle dot that separate it from the notice. English shows it in pieces as before (a merge group, output-and-languages §9.3); other languages show only the group’s .whole message.

zoomLevels.range.description: A run of zoom level keys, written as a range ("1–4").

zoomLevels.both.description: Hint for a selected zoom: what the zoom level keys do. {levels} is the keys ("1–4", or a list), {count} how many there are, {back} the key that pulls back ("0").

zoomLevels.levels.description: Hint for a selected zoom when no key pulls back: what the zoom level keys do. {levels} is the keys, {count} how many there are.

zoomLevels.back.description: Hint for a selected zoom when only the pull-back key has a shortcut: {back} is the key ("0").

reserved.pressesButton.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Enter"), which stays as it is.

reserved.movesBetweenControls.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Shift + Tab"), which stays as it is.

reserved.closesWindow.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Ctrl + W"), which stays as it is.

reserved.windowMenu.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Alt + Space"), which stays as it is.

reserved.startMenu.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Ctrl + Esc"), which stays as it is.

reserved.taskManager.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Ctrl + Shift + Esc"), which stays as it is.

reserved.switchesWindow.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Alt + Esc"), which stays as it is.

reserved.reloads.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Ctrl + Shift + R"), which stays as it is.

reserved.developerTools.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Ctrl + Shift + I"), which stays as it is.

reserved.fullScreen.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("F11"), which stays as it is.

reserved.resetsZoom.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Ctrl + 0"), which stays as it is.

reserved.zooms.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Ctrl + -"), which stays as it is.

reserved.escape.description: Shortcuts editor: why a key cannot be a shortcut, shown under the command when the user presses it. {keys} is the key ("Esc"), which stays as it is.

check.unusable.description: Shortcuts editor: the key pressed cannot be a shortcut at all.

check.needsModifier.description: Shortcuts editor: a shortcut for a command that also works in text fields must use Ctrl or Alt. {keys} is the key pressed. Ctrl and Alt are keycaps.

dialog.removeLabel.description: Shortcuts editor: accessible name of the x on a shortcut chip. {keys} is the keycaps, {command} the command's title.

dialog.removeTitle.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of the x on a shortcut chip.

dialog.stepKey.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of a key a nudge command borrows from a step command while timeline items are selected; {command} is the step command's title.

dialog.standardKey.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of a standard Windows key (Ctrl + C and the like) that works for a command while no command has it.

dialog.captureLabel.description: Shortcuts editor: accessible name of the button that records a shortcut; {command} is the command's title.

dialog.captureTitle.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of the button that records a shortcut. Esc is a keycap.

dialog.pressKeys.description: Shortcuts editor: shown in the button while it waits for a shortcut to be pressed.

dialog.addLabel.description: Shortcuts editor: accessible name of the + button of a command; {command} is its title.

dialog.full.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of the + button when a command has the most shortcuts it can have; {n} is that number (4).

dialog.addTitle.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of the + button of a command.

dialog.resetLabel.description: Shortcuts editor: accessible name of the button that puts a command's shortcuts back to its defaults; {command} is its title.

dialog.resetTo.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of the reset button of a changed command; {keys} is its default shortcuts, as keycaps ("Ctrl + Shift + Z or Ctrl + Y").

dialog.resetToNone.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of the reset button of a changed command that has no shortcut by default.

dialog.isDefault.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of the reset button while a command has its default shortcuts.

dialog.usedBy.description: Shortcuts editor: follows the keycaps of a shortcut another command has ("Ctrl + Z is used by Undo."); {command} is that command's title, in bold.

dialog.useHere.description: Shortcuts editor: button of the question about a shortcut another command has: take it for this command.

dialog.search.description: Shortcuts editor: accessible name of the search field.

dialog.searchPlaceholder.description: Shortcuts editor: placeholder of the search field.

dialog.noMatch.description: Shortcuts editor: shown when nothing matches the search; {query} is what the user typed.

dialog.pauseHint.description: Shortcuts editor: note at the foot of the dialog. Esc, Enter and Tab are keycaps.

dialog.resetAllTitle.description: Shortcuts editor: tooltip of Reset all.

dialog.resetAll.description: Shortcuts editor: button that puts every command's shortcuts back to the defaults.

dialog.takeBack.description: Shortcuts editor: button of the question shown when a command is reset while other commands have its default shortcuts: give them back to this command. {count} is how many shortcuts (never 0).

undoHint.whole.description: The Undo shortcut after a notice about a big change, as a phrase of its own; {keys} is the keycap (Ctrl + Z). The app puts it after the notice with a " · " separator. Used only when the UI language is not English (merge group, output-and-languages §9.3): English builds the same sentence from its pieces.
